destination.title: Calabi–Yau geometry, computation and compactification physics
destination.question: How can Calabi–Yau geometries, their moduli and quantum corrections be constructed and computed, and what do these data establish about compactification physics?
destination.summary: A proposed parent connects geometric construction, mirror and period calculations, degeneration theory, internal metrics and their physical applications. Existing target questions provide the public directions; numerical review batches remain provenance. No original prose definition of the numerical parent was supplied, so this authored scope requires independent review.

systems: Calabi–Yau geometries, with dimensions and construction classes retained by source
Specified Type II, heterotic, M-theory and F-theory compactifications
Local geometries, GLSMs and related special-geometric or conformal descriptions where explicitly connected
targets: Geometric construction, classification and model searches
Periods, mirror maps, special geometry and quantum couplings
Degenerations, distances, towers, singularities and quantum phases
Charged spectra, black objects, symmetries and arithmetic consistency questions
Internal metrics, spectra, normalized interactions and decoupling diagnostics
Geometric inputs to effective theories, stabilization and inflation
regimes: Source-specific classical, perturbative, nonperturbative and numerical treatments
Finite- and infinite-distance limits, with volume and hierarchy conditions retained
Fixed-modulus calculations and explicitly moduli-dependent approximations
assumptions: Related targets need not share a system, mechanism or approximation.
Conjectures, proposed extensions and reported example calculations retain their source-specific status.
Approximation accuracy and physical control depend on the observable.
Child-ledger support is attributed evidence, not a parent rereading of descendants.
conventions: Internal Ricci-flat metrics, effective moduli-space metrics and matter kinetic metrics are distinct.
Calabi–Yau dimension, spacetime dimension, parameter count and approximation degree remain separate.
Period reconstruction, charge bounds and flux stabilization can be distinct contributions of one source unit.
Existing overview overlap does not establish fine-question equivalence.
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland geometry and compactification work
Analytic, conventional numerical and machine-learning methods
Mathematical questions about Calabi–Yau geometry and its moduli
Explicitly qualified method, application and comparison routes to adjacent subjects
excludes: Generic programming-language design as a direct Calabi–Yau physics result
Automatic compactification interpretations for Feynman-integral motives or generic integrable models
Universal accuracy, consistency, vacuum existence or classification claims inferred from restricted examples
Automatic admission of child questions still requiring adjudication

evidence.text: How can asymptotic Hodge theory organize Calabi–Yau periods and physical couplings near degenerations, enabling calculations of weak-gravity bounds and flux-moduli stabilization beyond large complex structure?

sources.title: Lectures on Numerical and Machine Learning Methods for Approximating Ricci-flat Calabi-Yau Metrics

evidence.text: How can conventional numerical algorithms and neural networks approximate Ricci-flat metrics on compact Calabi–Yau manifolds, with sufficient accuracy and moduli dependence for string compactification applications?

sources.title: Non-birational twisted derived equivalences in abelian GLSMs

evidence.text: How can abelian GLSMs realize non-birational Kähler phases, and can homological projective duality (HPD) explain their geometric, Landau–Ginzburg, and noncommutative descriptions?

sources.title: Recent developments in heterotic compactifications

evidence.text: Does mirror symmetry extend from target spaces to heterotic target-bundle pairs, exchanging sheaf cohomology and quantum-corrected computations?

sources.title: Euler Characteristics of Crepant Resolutions of Weierstrass Models

evidence.text: How can one compute Euler characteristics of crepant resolutions of singular Weierstrass G-models over smooth bases of arbitrary dimension, and specialize these results to Calabi–Yau Euler characteristics and threefold Hodge numbers?

sources.title: Exact Computation of the Special Geometry for Calabi–Yau Hypersurfaces of Fermat Type

evidence.text: Can the special Kähler potential be computed explicitly for all polynomial complex-structure deformations of Fermat Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces, including the real structure needed to pair their periods?

sources.title: The Kreuzer-Skarke Axiverse

evidence.text: How do Kähler-cone constraints at large Picard number affect cycle volumes, control of the α′ expansion, and the masses and geometric field ranges of axions in Calabi–Yau compactifications?

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: What geometric degeneration accompanies a gauge symmetry becoming global in an elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau compactification? The supplied limit sends the gauge-support volume to infinity along a nef isotropic direction of the base Kähler cone.

sources.title: Infinite Distance Networks in Field Space and Charge Orbits

evidence.text: How can the towers expected at infinite distance be identified throughout a Calabi–Yau complex-structure moduli space, including intersections of singular divisors and different paths approaching those intersections?

sources.title: Infinite Distance Networks in Field Space and Charge Orbits

evidence.text: How do infinite-distance loci in Calabi–Yau complex-structure moduli space intersect, and can their monodromy and Hodge-theoretic data identify candidate towers for the Swampland Distance Conjecture, including the dependence on approach paths?

sources.title: Swampland Distance Conjecture for One-Parameter Calabi-Yau Threefolds

evidence.text: Does approaching each infinite-distance boundary in these Calabi–Yau moduli spaces produce infinitely many stable particles with exponentially decreasing masses?

sources.title: Emergent strings from infinite distance limits

evidence.text: How does a finite-volume Kähler degeneration select a shrinking curve or surface fiber?

sources.title: Emergent strings from infinite distance limits

evidence.text: Which asymptotic shapes of a Calabi–Yau three-fold allow some internal cycles to expand and others to collapse at finite total volume?

sources.title: Classifying Calabi–Yau Threefolds Using Infinite Distance Limits

evidence.text: Can the complete pattern of infinite-volume degenerations furnish a practical invariant grouping Calabi–Yau threefolds, distinguishing some homotopy types and exposing elliptic, K3 and nested fibrations?

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: How can the full Hodge filtration on primitive middle cohomology be represented near a Calabi–Yau fourfold degeneration where several local complex-structure coordinates approach i∞?

sources.title: GLSM for Calabi-Yau Manifolds of Berglund-Hubsch Type

evidence.text: How can special Kähler geometry for polynomial deformations of Berglund–Hübsch-type Calabi–Yau manifolds be computed from Landau–Ginzburg data, and can a mirror GLSM sphere partition function reproduce the resulting exponentiated Kähler potential?

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which Calabi–Yau threefold compactifications can avoid world-sheet instanton corrections? The section permits finite free quotients of tori and elliptic-curve–K3 products, so its geometric domain extends beyond simply connected threefolds of strict SU(3) holonomy.

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which special Kähler geometries admit quantum-consistent UV completions, and can their arithmetic structure unify and strengthen the N=2 swampland conditions?

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Do physical and motivic realizability select the same subset of formal special geometries?

sources.title: Sphere Partition Function of Calabi–Yau GLSMs

evidence.text: Can the exact sphere partition function of Calabi-Yau GLSMs be expressed using a common structure in geometric, Landau-Ginzburg and hybrid phases, with identifiable state spaces, pairings, Gamma classes and Givental I/J-functions?

sources.title: Attractors are not algebraic

evidence.text: Does the Hodge-theoretic attractor condition force algebraic moduli for Calabi–Yau varieties, as proposed in the higher-dimensional analogue of Moore's threefold Attractor Conjecture?

sources.title: Weak gravity bounds in asymptotic string compactifications

evidence.text: How do complex-structure degenerations constrain charged BPS states and electric BPS black-hole extremality in four-dimensional N=2 Calabi–Yau compactifications?

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: When do hyperbolic toy geometries describe actual infinite-distance regions of compactification moduli spaces?

sources.title: Moduli-dependent Calabi-Yau and SU(3)-structure metrics from Machine Learning

evidence.text: How can explicit Calabi–Yau metrics be approximated while retaining complex-structure dependence? The appendices distinguish the modulus ψ, which changes the geometry, from the section degree k, which controls the algebraic approximation at fixed geometry.

sources.title: Moduli-dependent KK towers and the swampland distance conjecture on the quintic Calabi-Yau manifold

evidence.text: Do lightening and crossings persist for forms, other moduli directions, and other Calabi–Yau constructions, and can the crossing pattern be predicted?

sources.title: Swampland conjectures and infinite flop chains

evidence.text: Do topology-changing flop trajectories provide large physical moduli distances without a tower of light states? The relevant distinction is between repeated descriptions of finitely many Calabi–Yau geometries and genuinely infinitely many isomorphism classes.

sources.title: Mathematical Structures of Non-perturbative Topological String Theory: From GW to DT Invariants

evidence.text: How do directional Borel sums of the resolved-conifold Gromov–Witten potential encode Donaldson–Thomas invariants, Riemann–Hilbert problems and BPS wall crossing at weak and strong topological string coupling?

sources.title: Learning Size and Shape of Calabi-Yau Spaces

evidence.text: Can neural networks efficiently approximate Ricci-flat Calabi–Yau metrics for user-specified shape and size moduli, and can inexpensive Monge–Ampère training substitute for direct curvature optimization?

sources.title: Finiteness for self-dual classes in integral variations of Hodge structure

evidence.text: Does the finiteness theorem for integral Hodge classes of fixed self-intersection extend to integral classes preserved by the Weil operator in a polarized variation of Hodge structure?

sources.title: Calabi–Yau metrics, energy functionals and machine learning

evidence.text: Can supervised neural-network learning approximate the Kähler-potential data of Headrick–Nassar optimal numerical Calabi–Yau metrics accurately from a small training sample, with reduced computational time?

sources.title: Non-birational twisted derived equivalences in abelian GLSMs

evidence.text: The physical analysis uses D/F-term constraints, integration of massive quadratic fields, and a fermion-zero-mode Berry calculation. K-theoretic monodromy provides indirect consistency evidence: for X, (M_0^2−1)^4=0 while lower positive powers remain nonzero.

sources.title: Recent developments in heterotic compactifications

evidence.text: Translate BRST operators into cohomology, count scalar and vector zero modes, insert the obstruction class when necessary, and integrate on the classical or instanton moduli space.

sources.title: Euler Characteristics of Crepant Resolutions of Weierstrass Models

evidence.text: Compute χ(Y) as the degree of c(TY)∩[Y]. Obtain Chern classes using explicit ambient blowups, Aluffi’s complete-intersection blowup formula and adjunction; push successively through the blowups and then through the ambient projective bundle to B.

sources.title: Exact Computation of the Special Geometry for Calabi–Yau Hypersurfaces of Fermat Type

evidence.text: Introduce twisted differentials D± = d ± dW0∧ and dual relative cycles. Expand the deformation-dependent exponential, reduce monomials modulo twisted-exact forms, and express the resulting coefficients through Pochhammer symbols and gamma functions.

sources.title: The Kreuzer-Skarke Axiverse

evidence.text: Use minimum-volume bases of inherited effective divisors to bound instanton suppression. Obtain field-range upper bounds by trivializing a full-rank charge subblock and bounding distances using the largest eigenvalue of its transformed kinetic metric.

sources.title: Tensionless Strings and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Allocate excitation among factors in proportion to their positive indices, then control integer rounding. For Jacobi products this yields a candidate large-level charge, whose survival still requires a nonzero final coefficient.

evidence.text: How does mirror symmetry determine the quantum Kähler geometry of two-parameter Calabi–Yau threefolds, particularly singular boundary loci, the large complex structure limit, mirror maps, and genus-zero and genus-one instanton contributions?

sources.title: F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: D-brane DBI reduction determines field-dependent kinetic terms and potentials; canonical normalization changes their asymptotic powers. T-duality relates massive Wilson lines to brane positions in flux backgrounds.

sources.title: F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: Kaluza–Klein reduction on non-harmonic forms satisfying dηp=kωp+1 produces axion-dependent internal field strengths. Reduction of the dual potential exposes a massive three-form coupled to a two-form.

sources.title: F-term Axion Monodromy Inflation

evidence.text: The F-term interpretation uses a three-form supermultiplet and a superspace coupling proportional to ∫d²θ ΦS. Domain-wall tensions and generalized calibrations provide a complementary superpotential description.
